title: SCIM resilient provisioning & deprovisioning with retries and audit hooks
creator: Asha Kapoor
description:
Goal: Implement SCIM provisioning improvements for SSO/SAML integrations to make user/group synces resilient, auditable, and compatible with RBAC v2 and admin controls. This ticket covers: 1) reliable user and group create/update/delete flows, 2) deterministic deprovisioning semantics (soft-delete + scheduled hard delete), 3) exponential-backoff retry engine with idempotency keys, 4) rich audit logging hooks (who initiated, source SCIM ID, before/after deltas), and 5) admin console controls for retry/force-sync/manual reconciliations.

Background: Several enterprise customers reported missing group membership updates and orphaned users after transient SCIM errors with their IdPs. We need to harden the provisioning layer used by SAML/SSO connectors and integrate with RBAC v2 so role assignments follow group changes. The platform must provide clear audit trails for compliance reviews.

Scope: - SCIM users: support create, replace, patch, delete, suspend. Ensure operations are idempotent using scimOperationId header and deterministic conflict resolution. - SCIM groups: hierarchical group imports, membership diffs, handle large group pagination. - Deprovisioning: implement soft-deactivate flag when SCIM delete received; start configurable grace window (default 14 days) before final hard delete. Provide admin override to immediately hard delete. Emit change events for RBAC v2 to revoke tokens and cached sessions. - Retries: implement a queue-based retry with exponential backoff (E.g., 1m, 5m, 20m, 2h, 12h) and a max attempts counter. Permanent failure classification for 4xx SCIM responses vs transient 5xx/network. - Idempotency and dedupe: use scimOperationId + provider id to prevent duplicate processing on retries/resends. - Audit logging: structured audit entries for each SCIM operation and subsequent reconciliation actions: fields must include event_id, timestamp, actor (IdP connector / admin), scim_resource_type, scim_id, internal_user_id, delta_summary, outcome (success/partial/failure), attempt_count, retry_policy_used. Logs should be emitted to existing audit pipeline with tag scim-provisioning. - Admin Controls: add UI endpoints to list pending retries, force re-run, cancel retry, and view last N diffs. RBAC controls: only users with security_admin role may perform force/hard-delete. - Metrics/Monitoring: instrument counters for ops/sec, retry attempts, permanent failures, mean time to reconcile, backlog size. Add dashboards and alerts for retry queue growth and repeated failures per connector.

Design notes: - We will persist a SCIM operation record in provisioning.store with status enum {pending, in_progress, succeeded, failed_transient, failed_permanent, cancelled, soft_deleted, hard_deleted}. This backs idempotency and retries. - Reconciliation worker reads pending operations and executes with circuit-breaker per-connector to avoid thundering herd. - On group syncs, emit user-level diffs rather than full user updates where possible to limit churn in KV caches and token revocations. - For deprovision semantics, we choose soft-deactivate -> scheduled hard delete because customers need a recover window; config toggle per-tenant to hard-delete immediately for sensitive environments. - For RBAC v2, group -> role mapping rules are applied in a deterministic post-provision step; failures there must surface to admin UI and do not block SCIM success.

Acceptance criteria: - SCIM flows succeed end-to-end in integration tests against a test IdP simulator for create/update/delete with intermittent 50% network failures. - Retry queue persists across service restarts and backoff schedule observed. - Admin UI shows pending retries and allows force-run; role-based access enforced by RBAC v2. - Audit logs contain required structured fields and are queryable for a given scim_id. - Migration plan to switch existing connectors to new provisioning path with zero user downtime.

Security and compliance: Include KMS for sensitive audit payloads retention policy, ensure PII minimization in logs (store internal_user_id, not email where possible). Security review required before rollout.

Rollout plan: 1) implement worker + persistence and unit tests behind feature flag (private-2026.03) 2) internal dogfood with 2 pilot customers and SAML test IdPs, enable soft-delete grace window default 14d 3) monitor metrics for 2 weeks, iterate on backoff constants 4) flip feature flag for all hosted connectors, add migration job to reconcile historical pending operations 5) document in Admin Guide and update SDKs.

Links and artifacts: - Design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/SEC/SCIM+Resilient+Provisioning - Prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/4321 - RBAC v2 mapping spec: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/PLAT/RBAC+v2+mapping - Audit schema: https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/audit-schemas

Notes on trade-offs: - We accept additional storage and complexity for operation records to gain reliability and auditability. - Soft-delete increases retention liabilities; we add tenant config and clear guidance in admin UI. - We prefer eventual consistency for group->role propagation to avoid locking in high-throughput group syncs, but provide immediate reconciliation via admin force-run where necessary.
comments: 2026-03-10 - Asha Kapoor: Ticket created after customer postmortem for ACME Corp. Initial requirements reviewed with PM and Security. Decided on soft-delete default.

2026-03-11 - Liam O'Connor: Spike completed for idempotency key design and queue persistence. Prototype stores operations in PostgreSQL with JSONB diffs. Raised potential scale issue for huge group diffs.
2026-03-12 - Priya Menon (Security): Reviewed audit field set. Requested inclusion of attempt_count and connector_request_id. Marked security_review_required.
2026-03-13 - Engineering review: Agreed to add circuit-breaker per connector and to classify 409 as permanent failure for duplicate requests. Action: ENG-4702 to add connector throttling metrics.

2026-03-14 - Liam O'Connor: Implemented retry worker skeleton and added metric scaffolding. Open PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/4389. Running unit tests locally; next: integration tests with IdP simulator.
